tables.name: User

fields.name: username
fields.note: CharField, unique compatibility identifier if retaining AbstractUser; generated/internal when login is email.

fields.name: is_active
fields.note: Django account flags. Platform root is `is_superuser=True`.

fields.name: is_staff
fields.note: Django account flags. Platform root is `is_superuser=True`.

fields.name: is_superuser
fields.note: Django account flags. Platform root is `is_superuser=True`.

tables.constraints: Relations: memberships, optional employee links, and actor/audit relations. Deactivate accounts instead of deleting them.

tables.name: CompanyMembership

fields.name: role
fields.note: CharField choices: owner, company_admin, hr, manager, payroll_manager, employee, auditor.

fields.name: status
fields.note: CharField choices: invited, active, suspended, ended.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(company, user)`; departments selected in scope must belong to a selected/allowed branch and the same company. The two M2M fields create implicit junction tables unless later replaced by an explicit scope model.

tables.name: Company
tables.constraints: Relations: root of all tenant-owned rows; CompanyMembership, Branch, CompanyFeature, CompanySubscription, settings, employees, and operational records.

tables.name: Feature

fields.name: code
fields.note: CharField, unique, such as attendance, leave, payroll.

fields.name: is_core
fields.note: BooleanField; core features cannot be removed from eligible packages.

tables.constraints: Relations: PackageFeature, CompanyFeature, AccessPermission.

tables.name: CompanyFeature

fields.name: limits
fields.note: JSONField for feature-specific scalar limits, validated by feature.

tables.constraints: Constraints: prevent overlapping active overrides for the same company/feature/effect. Effective access combines package snapshot and this dated override.

tables.name: Branch

fields.name: device_attendance_scope_override
fields.note: nullable CharField: assigned_devices, department_devices, branch_devices, company_devices; null inherits CompanyAttendanceSettings. This is the employee's assigned/home branch policy, not the source device branch's policy.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(company, code)`; one active default branch per company.

tables.name: Department
tables.constraints: Relations: Designation, CompanyDepartment.

tables.name: Designation
tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(department, code)`; unique `(department, name)`.

tables.name: CompanyDepartment

fields.name: head
fields.note: nullable FK -> Employee, PROTECT. The employee who administers permissions for everyone in this department.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(branch, department)` — a branch adopts each catalogue department at most once; the branch must belong to the same company.

tables.name: CompanyDesignation
tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(company_department, designation)`; the catalogue title's department must match the adoption row's catalogue department.

tables.name: Employee

fields.name: employment_status
fields.note: applicant, active, probation, suspended, resigned, terminated, retired.

fields.name: metadata
fields.note: JSONField for validated company-specific non-core attributes.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(company, user)` when user is not null. All business history references this permanent identity.

tables.name: EmployeeAssignment

fields.name: employee_code
fields.note: CharField; manually entered reusable business code.

fields.name: department
fields.note: FK -> CompanyDepartment, PROTECT. The company's adoption row, never the catalogue row.

fields.name: device_attendance_scope_override
fields.note: nullable CharField: assigned_devices, department_devices, branch_devices, company_devices; null inherits the assigned branch/company policy. This employee-level override lives on dated assignment history; changing it closes the old interval and creates its successor.

tables.constraints: Constraints: the adopted department belongs to the assignment's branch; the adopted designation belongs to that department; manager is not the employee; no overlapping active periods for one employee; no overlapping occupancy of `(company, employee_code)`. The same code may be reused after the earlier interval ends.

tables.name: EmployeeCompensation
tables.constraints: Constraints: positive base rate; currency matches company policy; non-overlapping active compensation ranges per employee.

fields.name: action
fields.note: view, create, edit, approve, finalize, pay, manage.

tables.name: DesignationPermission
tables.constraints: Constraints: unique effective rule per designation/permission at any instant; a title may not be ALLOWED what its own department DENIES through DepartmentPermission (86). That department ceiling replaced the old designation parent-chain walk.

tables.name: EmployeePermissionOverride
tables.constraints: Constraints: a GRANT may not exceed what the employee's current department DENIES — this is what makes delegating to a department head safe, since the head cannot widen the boundary they administer inside; selected departments belong to selected branches/company.

tables.name: DepartmentPermission

fields.name: can_delegate
fields.note: BooleanField; whether the department head may pass this on.

tables.constraints: Constraints: one effective rule per department/permission at any instant; end after start.

tables.name: Shift

fields.name: scheduled_minutes
fields.note: PositiveIntegerField; validated against times and breaks or calculated snapshot.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(company, code)`; timing and minute thresholds must be internally consistent.

tables.name: DepartmentShift
tables.constraints: Constraints: no overlapping duplicate department/shift assignments; at most one default at a time. In single-shift company mode all active department shifts must reference the company shift.

tables.name: EmployeeShiftAssignment
tables.constraints: Constraints: no overlapping effective assignments for an employee. Validate department eligibility except for an authorized override.

tables.name: CompanyAttendanceSettings

fields.name: company
fields.note: O2O -> Company, PROTECT, primary tenant owner.

fields.name: device_attendance_scope
fields.note: CharField: assigned_devices, department_devices, branch_devices, company_devices; default assigned_devices. Effective precedence: EmployeeAssignment override, assigned Branch override, company setting.

tables.constraints: Constraint: company_shift required only in single-shift mode. Historical AttendanceRecord snapshots preserve rules actually used.

tables.name: WeeklyOffRule

fields.name: branch
fields.note: nullable FK -> Branch, PROTECT; null means company-wide.

tables.constraints: Constraints: prevent overlapping duplicate weekday rules for the same company/branch.

tables.name: Holiday

fields.name: branch
fields.note: nullable FK -> Branch, PROTECT; null means company-wide.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique active holiday per `(company, branch, holiday_date)`, treating null branch as a comparable company-wide scope.

tables.name: HolidayWorkAssignment

fields.name: treatment
fields.note: normal_workday, overtime, compensatory_leave, overtime_and_comp_leave when explicitly allowed.

tables.constraints: Constraints: exactly one applicable source (dated holiday or recurring weekly-off rule); source applies on work_date; one active assignment per employee/work_date/source.

tables.name: DeviceVendor

fields.name: adapter_key
fields.note: CharField selecting a reviewed application adapter, never executable user input.

tables.constraints: Relations: DeviceModel and optional BiometricTemplate format metadata.

tables.name: DeviceModel

fields.name: capabilities
fields.note: JSONField, validated flags for push, face, fingerprint, card, commands, template export/import.

fields.name: supported_template_formats
fields.note: JSONField list of stable format/version codes.

tables.constraints: Constraint: unique `(vendor, model_code)`.

tables.name: BiometricDevice

fields.name: authentication_secret_hash
fields.note: password/hash field; never return the secret after enrollment.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(company, serial_number)`; device branch belongs to company.

tables.name: DeviceDepartment

fields.name: department
fields.note: FK -> CompanyDepartment, PROTECT. Not the catalogue row: a device belongs to one company's department in one branch.

tables.constraints: Constraints: device and department have the same company and branch; no overlapping duplicate mapping. This is the explicit through table for `BiometricDevice.departments`. Active mappings restrict department_devices mode; no active mappings means a shared branch device in that mode. These mappings do not additionally restrict branch_devices/company_devices mode or an explicit assigned-device grant.

tables.name: DeviceEnrollment

fields.name: device_user_id
fields.note: CharField exactly as stored by the device.

fields.name: attendance_enabled
fields.note: BooleanField, default true; a per-enrollment master switch. False excludes punches under every device scope, even company_devices. Evaluate historical value at punch time.

fields.name: assigned_device_authorized
fields.note: BooleanField, default false; explicit permission for assigned_devices mode. Wider department/branch/company scopes do not require this flag. Creating an enrollment for recognition alone does not grant restricted-mode attendance permission.

tables.constraints: Constraints: no overlapping use of one `(device, device_user_id)`; no overlapping duplicate employee/device authorization; resolve historical mapping using the punch timestamp. Enrollment identity, master enablement, and explicit assigned-device grant are separate concerns. Keep historical authorization changes in the audit trail; see DEVICE_ATTENDANCE_POLICY.md.

tables.name: BiometricTemplate
tables.constraints: Constraints: checksum/employee/type/format duplicate detection; face has no finger_position. Database backups and application logs must protect the encrypted data and key references.

tables.name: DeviceEnrollmentTemplate
tables.constraints: Constraints: unique active `(device_enrollment, biometric_template)`; employee and compatibility must match enrollment/device.

tables.name: DeviceMessage

fields.name: branch
fields.note: FK -> Branch, PROTECT snapshot at receipt.

fields.name: message_type
fields.note: punch_batch, heartbeat, enrollment_result, command_result, device_info, unknown.

fields.name: idempotency_key
fields.note: nullable CharField; set only from a trustworthy adapter identity.

fields.name: occurred_at_device
fields.note: nullable DateTimeField retaining the interpreted device time.

fields.name: raw_payload_binary
fields.note: nullable BinaryField/private object reference for large payloads.

tables.constraints: Constraints: one raw representation must exist; reliable `(device, idempotency_key)` unique when non-null. A payload hash alone is not safe proof that two punches are identical.

tables.name: PunchEvent

fields.name: reported_direction
fields.note: nullable vendor value; informational because it is not trusted.

fields.name: raw_record
fields.note: JSONField/text snapshot of the individual source record.

fields.name: authorization_status
fields.note: authorized, unauthorized_device, unknown_employee, expired_enrollment, department_mismatch, branch_mismatch, enrollment_disabled, policy_unresolved.

fields.name: authorization_snapshot
fields.note: JSONField containing the effective scope, winning policy level, effective evaluation time, historical enablement/grant results, and decision reason. These are frozen evaluation facts, not authoritative live relationships. Update resolution metadata only with an audited revision; never rewrite raw source values.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(device_message, source_record_index)`; reliable vendor punch identity unique per device when present. Timestamp is never the sole unique key.

tables.name: PunchAllocation

fields.name: attendance_correction
fields.note: nullable FK -> AttendanceCorrection, PROTECT for approved manual input.

fields.name: event_at
fields.note: DateTimeField used by calculation; copied from punch or approved correction.

fields.name: exclusion_reason
fields.note: duplicate, unauthorized_device, outside_window, superseded, manual_exclusion, other.

tables.constraints: Constraints: exactly one source (PunchEvent or approved AttendanceCorrection); unique source per calculation version; sequence unique within attendance/version. Merge all authorized devices into one employee/shift stream ordered by event time; never restart alternating IN/OUT at each device or incoming batch.

tables.name: AttendanceSession
tables.constraints: Constraints: end after start; allocation directions correct; sequence unique per record/version. Both allocations belong to this attendance record and employee/company, but may originate from different devices. Never require matching device IDs.

tables.name: AttendanceRecord

fields.name: attendance_status
fields.note: present, absent, leave, holiday, weekly_off, incomplete, excused.

fields.name: is_payroll_locked
fields.note: BooleanField summary; authoritative lock belongs to finalized payroll.

tables.constraints: Constraint: unique `(company, employee, work_date)`; assignment applies on work date and department/branch match it.

fields.name: correction_type
fields.note: add_punch, replace_punch, remove_from_calculation, change_work_date, adjust_overtime, other.

fields.name: proposed_event_at
fields.note: nullable fields for structured manual input.

fields.name: proposed_direction
fields.note: nullable fields for structured manual input.

fields.name: status
fields.note: draft, submitted, approved, rejected, withdrawn, applied.

tables.name: AttendancePenaltyRule
tables.constraints: Constraint: rule inputs consistent with metric/method. Activated rule versions are immutable.

tables.name: PenaltyAssessment
tables.constraints: Constraint: unique occurrence identity per company; one original payroll posting.

tables.name: PenaltyAssessmentAttendance
tables.constraints: Constraint: unique `(penalty_assessment, attendance_record)`. This is the explicit M2M through table.

tables.name: LeaveType
tables.constraints: Constraint: unique `(company, code)`.

tables.name: LeavePolicy

fields.name: current_version
fields.note: nullable FK -> LeavePolicyVersion, PROTECT, set after version creation.

tables.constraints: Constraints: department requires matching branch; only one applicable default per scope. Avoid a migration cycle by adding current_version after the initial version table or treating it as a cached pointer.

tables.name: LeavePolicyVersion

fields.name: approval_route_definition
fields.note: validated JSONField referencing roles/designation rules by stable codes; actual approvers are materialized later.

fields.name: lfa_configuration
fields.note: validated JSONField; FK values such as SalaryComponent should be explicit nullable FKs where required.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(leave_policy, version_number)`; non-overlapping active effective periods. Freeze after use.

tables.name: LeavePolicyTypeRule
tables.constraints: Constraint: unique `(policy_version, leave_type)`; percentages and limits valid.

tables.name: EmployeeLeavePolicyAssignment
tables.constraints: Constraint: no overlapping explicit employee policy assignments.

tables.name: LeaveEntitlement
tables.constraints: Constraint: unique entitlement for employee/type/period/policy context; overlapping accounts for the same type require explicit migration/reconciliation.

tables.name: LeaveBalanceEntry

fields.name: entry_kind
fields.note: opening, accrual, manual_credit, manual_debit, reservation, reservation_release, usage, cancellation_reversal, expiry, carry_out, carry_in, encashment, compensatory_credit, reversal.

fields.name: source_grant
fields.note: nullable FK -> self, PROTECT for grant consumption.

tables.constraints: Constraints: nonzero balance or reservation delta; unique source key; one reversal per entry; source fields consistent with kind.

tables.name: LeaveRequest

fields.name: status
fields.note: draft, submitted, pending, approved, rejected, withdrawn, cancelled, partially_cancelled.

fields.name: submitted_by
fields.note: nullable FK -> User, SET_NULL; HR may submit for an employee.

tables.constraints: Constraints: amendment/cancellation needs original request with same company/employee; approved request requires segments and completed approvals.

tables.name: LeaveRequestSegment
tables.constraints: Constraints: duration-specific fields required; end not before start; no overlap with active segments for employee after expanding intervals.

tables.name: LeaveDay

fields.name: entitlement
fields.note: nullable FK -> LeaveEntitlement, PROTECT for tracked balances.

tables.constraints: Constraints: covered interval positive and within relevant work date/shift; active approved intervals do not overlap; pay type matches percentage.

tables.name: LeaveApprovalStep
tables.constraints: Constraints: exactly one target FK; unique target/stage/approver; decision fields required when decided.

tables.name: LeaveAttachment
tables.constraints: Constraint: exactly one target.

tables.name: LeaveEncashment

fields.name: status
fields.note: draft, submitted, approved, rejected, posted, cancelled, reversed.

tables.constraints: Constraint: approved units cannot exceed eligible available balance. Resulting payroll lines point back to this row, so reversals and off-cycle corrections remain possible.

tables.name: LeaveCompensatoryCredit

fields.name: status
fields.note: draft, submitted, approved, credited, rejected, cancelled, reversed.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique qualifying source/treatment; do not award overtime and leave together unless treatment explicitly permits it.

tables.name: LeaveFareAssistanceClaim

fields.name: status
fields.note: draft, submitted, approved, rejected, withdrawn, cancelled, posted, reversed.

tables.constraints: Constraints: same-company qualifying leave; policy eligibility; unique active occurrence slot per employee/benefit cycle. Resulting PayrollLine rows point back to the claim. LFA never changes LeaveEntitlement.

tables.name: PayrollSettings

fields.name: pay_frequency
fields.note: monthly initially; reserved choices may include weekly, biweekly, semimonthly.

fields.name: monthly_divisor
fields.note: DecimalField, default 30 for the agreed initial deduction basis.

tables.constraints: Constraint: unique `company` (implement as O2O semantics).

tables.name: PayrollPolicyVersion

fields.name: calculation_config
fields.note: JSONField for validated non-relational formula parameters.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(company, code, version_number)`; no overlapping active date ranges for the same code; activated versions are immutable.

tables.name: SalaryComponent

fields.name: subtype
fields.note: base_salary, overtime, bonus, allowance, absence, penalty, advance_recovery, loan_recovery, leave_encashment, lfa, tax, other.

fields.name: formula_expression
fields.note: blank TextField; use a restricted expression language, never Python eval.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(company, code)`; category and sign behavior must agree.

tables.name: SalaryStructure
tables.constraints:
Relations: components are M2M -> SalaryComponent through SalaryStructureComponent.
Constraints: unique `(company, code, version_number)`; at most one active default structure for a company/date; activated structures are immutable except retirement metadata.

tables.name: SalaryStructureComponent

fields.name: calculation_method
fields.note: fixed, employee_compensation, quantity_x_rate, percentage, formula, source_amount.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(salary_structure, salary_component)`; both belong to the same company; required operands depend on calculation method.

tables.name: EmployeeSalaryStructureAssignment
tables.constraints: Constraints: no overlapping active assignments for an employee; employee and structure belong to the same company.

tables.name: PayrollPeriod

fields.name: status
fields.note: draft, open, processing, closed, locked, cancelled.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(company, code)`; `period_start <= period_end`; regular periods of the same frequency should not overlap.

tables.name: PayrollRun

fields.name: source_run
fields.note: nullable FK -> self, PROTECT for correction/reversal.

fields.name: status
fields.note: draft, queued, calculating, review, approved, posted, failed, cancelled, reversed.

fields.name: generated_by
fields.note: nullable FK -> User, SET_NULL/PROTECT according to audit policy.

fields.name: approved_by
fields.note: nullable FK -> User, SET_NULL/PROTECT according to audit policy.

fields.name: posted_by
fields.note: nullable FK -> User, SET_NULL/PROTECT according to audit policy.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(company, idempotency_key)` and `(payroll_period, run_type, revision_number)`; only one posted regular result chain may be authoritative for an employee/period.

tables.name: PayrollRecord

fields.name: paid_amount
fields.note: DecimalField cached summaries; authoritative values come from payment allocations.

fields.name: outstanding_amount
fields.note: DecimalField cached summaries; authoritative values come from payment allocations.

fields.name: status
fields.note: draft, calculated, review, approved, posted, partially_paid, paid, void, reversed.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(payroll_run, employee)`; employee belongs to run company; totals equal active line sums and allocations cannot exceed payable balance.

tables.name: PayrollCompensationSegment

fields.name: segment_start
fields.note: DateField, inclusive dates within the payroll period.

fields.name: segment_end
fields.note: DateField, inclusive dates within the payroll period.

tables.constraints: Constraints: segment dates must fall inside the period, cannot overlap for the same PayrollRecord, and referenced history rows must cover the segment.

tables.name: PayrollDailyLine

fields.name: attendance_status
fields.note: present, absent, leave, mixed, incomplete, not_applicable.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(payroll_segment, work_date)`; all evidence belongs to the employee/company/date; fractions are nonnegative and bounded where applicable.

tables.name: PayrollLine

fields.name: source_type
fields.note: base_compensation, attendance, penalty, overtime, bonus, adjustment, advance_recovery, loan_repayment, leave_encashment, lfa, manual, reversal.

fields.name: original_line
fields.note: nullable FK -> self, PROTECT for reversals/corrections.

tables.constraints: Constraints: source fields must agree with `source_type`; at most one typed source for a normal line; prevent duplicate active posting from the same source/component/run; reversal lines reference an original and use the opposite financial effect.

tables.name: PayrollApprovalStep
tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(payroll_run, sequence)`; assignee must have company access; steps execute in order unless policy explicitly permits parallel stages.

tables.name: SalaryPayment

fields.name: status
fields.note: draft, pending, completed, failed, cancelled, refunded, reversed.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(company, payment_reference)` and `(company, idempotency_key)`; allocated amount cannot exceed completed payment amount.

tables.name: SalaryPaymentAllocation
tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(company, allocation_reference)`; payment and payroll record belong to the same employee/company/currency; active allocations cannot overallocate either side.

tables.name: SalaryAdvance

fields.name: status
fields.note: draft, submitted, approved, rejected, partially_disbursed, disbursed, recovering, settled, cancelled, written_off.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(company, request_reference)`; approved amount cannot exceed requested amount without explicit override; outstanding derives from disbursements minus applied recoveries/reversals.

tables.name: AdvanceDisbursement
tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(company, disbursement_reference)`; completed active disbursements cannot exceed approved advance amount.

tables.name: SalaryAdvanceRecovery

fields.name: status
fields.note: scheduled, posted, received, skipped, cancelled, reversed.

tables.constraints:
Relations: PayrollLine points to this row when method is payroll_deduction.
Constraints: unique `(company, idempotency_key)`; posted/received recoveries cannot exceed outstanding principal unless explicitly treated as a refundable overpayment.

tables.name: EmployeeLoan

fields.name: status
fields.note: draft, submitted, approved, rejected, partially_disbursed, active, suspended, settled, cancelled, written_off.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(company, loan_reference)`; balances reconcile to completed disbursements, repayments, and approved waivers/write-offs.

tables.name: LoanDisbursement
tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(company, disbursement_reference)`; completed disbursements cannot exceed approved principal.

tables.name: LoanInstallment

fields.name: status
fields.note: scheduled, partially_paid, paid, deferred, waived, cancelled.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(employee_loan, installment_number)`; component totals reconcile to total due; paid summaries derive from active allocations.

tables.name: LoanRepayment

fields.name: status
fields.note: pending, posted, received, failed, cancelled, reversed.

tables.constraints:
Relations: PayrollLine points to this row when method is payroll_deduction.
Constraints: unique `(company, repayment_reference)` and `(company, idempotency_key)`; allocations cannot exceed the active repayment amount.

tables.name: LoanRepaymentAllocation
tables.constraints: Constraints: repayment and installment belong to the same loan/company/currency; active allocations cannot exceed the repayment or remaining installment balances.

tables.name: PayrollAdjustment

fields.name: adjustment_type
fields.note: earning, deduction, correction, advance_waiver, loan_waiver, carry_forward.

fields.name: amount
fields.note: DecimalField money; store nonnegative and use type/direction for effect.

fields.name: status
fields.note: draft, submitted, approved, rejected, posted, cancelled, reversed.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(company, adjustment_reference)` and `(company, idempotency_key)`; target/source fields agree with adjustment type; a balance-only waiver must not silently create salary earnings.

tables.name: PayrollRemittance

fields.name: status
fields.note: draft, approved, submitted, completed, failed, cancelled, reversed.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(company, remittance_reference)` and `(company, idempotency_key)`; active allocations cannot exceed a completed remittance.

tables.name: PayrollRemittanceAllocation
tables.constraints: Constraints: remittance and line must have the same company/currency/provider-compatible component; active allocations cannot exceed either available remittance value or line liability.

tables.name: Package

fields.name: included_user_limit
fields.note: nullable PositiveIntegerField if login-seat pricing is later offered.

tables.constraints: Relations: features are M2M -> Feature through PackageFeature; CompanySubscription references Package.

tables.name: PackageFeature

fields.name: configuration
fields.note: JSONField for validated feature-specific commercial limits.

tables.constraints: Constraint: unique `(package, feature)`.

tables.name: CompanySubscription

fields.name: status
fields.note: trial, active, past_due, suspended, cancelled, expired.

fields.name: feature_snapshot
fields.note: JSONField immutable commercial snapshot of feature codes and limits.

tables.constraints: Constraints: unique `(company, subscription_reference)`; normally no overlapping active/trial subscriptions; entitlements use the subscription snapshot plus explicit CompanyFeature overrides. Capacity counting policy must define whether employees, users, or both are billable—the current recommendation is active employees.

fields.name: company
fields.note: nullable FK -> Company, PROTECT; null only for platform-level actions.

fields.name: action
fields.note: CharField stable code such as employee.updated or payroll_run.posted.

fields.name: object_app
fields.note: CharField identifiers; use content types only if their operational tradeoff is accepted.

fields.name: object_model
fields.note: CharField identifiers; use content types only if their operational tradeoff is accepted.

fields.name: object_id
fields.note: CharField identifiers; use content types only if their operational tradeoff is accepted.

fields.name: object_public_id
fields.note: CharField identifiers; use content types only if their operational tradeoff is accepted.

tables.name: CompanyMembership_allowed_branches
tables.constraints: Unique pair; both rows must belong to the same company. Tenant ownership is inherited from the source parent; this implicit junction has no company_id.

tables.name: CompanyMembership_allowed_departments
tables.constraints: Unique pair; both rows must belong to the same company. Tenant ownership is inherited from the source parent; this implicit junction has no company_id.

tables.name: EmployeePermissionOverride_allowed_branches
tables.constraints: Unique pair; both rows must belong to the same company. Tenant ownership is inherited from the source parent; this implicit junction has no company_id.

tables.name: EmployeePermissionOverride_allowed_departments
tables.constraints: Unique pair; both rows must belong to the same company. Tenant ownership is inherited from the source parent; this implicit junction has no company_id.

tables.name: PayrollDailyLine_leave_days
tables.constraints: Unique pair; both rows must belong to the same company. Tenant ownership is inherited from the source parent; this implicit junction has no company_id.
